q: I can’t sleep even when he sleeps. I work 5 days a week, 8 hours shifts as a nurse and I’m struggling in my career as well.
cx: Five months after a second birth; baby sleeps about eight hours a night.
r: mental health (post centred on postpartum depression)

q: my husband has tried to take the wakes and soothe back to sleep but he cries so hard it keeps me up and I hate him crying more than like 10 mins so I usually tell dad to bring him to me and I latch him to calm him down then he falls asleep. this is not sustainable - I’m so sleep deprived.
cx: Ten-month-old wakes six to eight times a night and refuses a bottle at night.

q: I see every number on the clock overnight and it sucks walking between rooms all night
cx: Baby starts in his own room and wakes hourly.

q: The whole three last days, slept on average of 4-5 hours each night and woke up every hour to pee. My body is feeling hot, gassy, and exhausted.
cx: At 36 weeks on a business trip three hours from home.

q: Thought I’d get the best sleep finally. Nope- I woke up after 2 hours of sleep, sweating and feeling bloated. Peed. Did some stretches to release gas. Drank some water and now my whole body feels so hot and I am so dizzy I can’t sleep. I have to wake up in 3 hours and a half to get to the client.
cx: The hotel night she posted from.

q: Just wanted to rant. I am so tired… could be worse I know. But it’s just I am so tired.
cx: How she closes the post about her hotel night.

q: I’m breastfeeding (99% exclusively but also pumping to get a break now and again), and almost every evening since she hit 5 weeks she’s cluster feeding for around 5 or so hours. […] She’s up 3 or 4 times which doesn’t seem like much, but because each time it can be around an hour until she’s asleep enough to put her back in her crib, it doesn’t give me much time to sleep.
cx: Six weeks after an emergency c-section and NICU stay.
r: mental health (post titled about mental health)

q: I’m absolutely exhausted and I go back to work in 6 weeks, which is starting to make me panic a bit. […] How did you cope with this level of sleep deprivation? Did you just accept it and wait it out? Did anything make your days easier?
cx: Ten-month-old has never slept through; not interested in sleep training.

q: I work 3 12s as a nurse and am exhausted on my days off either recovering or chasing after my toddler […] also considering having baby #2… what worked for you managing being pregnant on night shift (managing exhaustion, nausea, etc.)
cx: Asks other mothers on night shift how they cope.

q: Last night, she was waking up screaming every 15 minutes. By 4 a.m., I was so exhausted that I ended up trying CIO. She screamed until 7 a.m., when it was time to get her up, and never went back to sleep. I’m extremely sleep deprived and honestly at a loss.
cx: Second baby, four-month regression with reflux and allergy.

q: Her longest stretch of sleep in the past week has been about 2 hours. My husband and I are having to sleep in shifts just to function.
cx: Four-month-old who wakes at 9pm screaming after the last bottle.

q: During the weekends he sleeps until 2pm or 3pm meanwhile I've been up with the kids since 7:30-8am, cleaning the house, laundry, cooking breakfast/lunch, snacks upon snacks.
cx: 31 weeks pregnant with a fifth child; husband works evenings.

q: We just got back from a family vacation with my family and while sleeping beauty got his rest I was with the kids. My family helped somewhat but kept making comments about him sleeping and it was pissing me off more like yeah no crap this is what I deal with.
cx: Family remarks about her husband sleeping late on holiday.

q: Just this morning, he set his alarm four times to "come with me" to drop off the kids at summer camp, but he slept through and after getting 4 kids up and ready, and running behind I just left and dropped off kids solo.
cx: The morning that made her post.

q: I've woken him up multiple times and then he's in a pissy mood and says he's not a morning person and it makes for rough day for me. But I'm like you're a freaking parent welcome to being a morning person I am EXHAUSTED TO. I've had naps here and there but they aren't restful as the kids flock to me.
cx: Replies to a commenter suggesting she wake him.

q: First trimester I was sooo tired, sleeping wasn’t an issue at all. Now that I’m in the second trimester, I’m still exhausted during the day, but at night I have insomnia. Unisom is not helping by the way.
cx: Asks for anything that helps her sleep.

q: And my sweet girl has been sleeping through the night for 3 months now. We’re in a routine and I’m still struggling. I’m at least sleeping more but lots of anxiety around going to bed.
cx: Seven months after a fourth baby; long recovery from postpartum anxiety.
r: mental health (post centred on postpartum anxiety and treatment)

q: Everyone tells me things get better around 6 months but I'm struggling to believe it.
cx: First-time mother of a five-month-old, opening her post.

q: for the first 6 weeks of his life LO woke every 45 minutes overnight and my husband and I slept in shifts. By 8 weeks this had extended to every 2-3 hours but he started fighting naps (all five of them per day) and bedtime, so I spent more than half my day trapped in a dark room rocking and bouncing him while desperately trying not to fall asleep myself.
cx: Her first five months, step by step.

q: I go to bed with my baby at 7:30 just to snatch as much sleep as I can. During the day he only ever naps in 30 minute spurts, which gives me just enough time to eat, cat nap, or couch rot (but never all 3). I have no life.
cx: How she fits her own sleep around the baby's.

q: I always thought my maternity leave would be this golden time in my life where I'd cuddle blissfully with my baby and bake and maybe pick up a new hobby (lol) but obviously that isn't the case. I'm so grateful to live in Canada and have my 12-18 months, but the truth is I haven't really enjoyed any of it and I feel so guilty and ashamed for that.
cx: Five months into a long Canadian leave.

q: Even though my husband assures me "he's just a baby" I feel like it's my fault for not being able to optimize his sleep needs.
cx: She tracks wake windows trying to fix the baby's sleep.

q: I’ll be going back to work full time in 2 weeks. When my husband is gone, he gets a full nights sleep, his company pays for any food he wants, and I’m stuck at home running on 5 hours on a good night
cx: Husband travels for work; she is alone with an 11-week-old after a c-section.

q: I’ve asked my mom to help clean and she just comes over and holds the baby and just asks me what to do the entire time and I don’t have the mental capacity to direct her on what to do.
cx: What help from her parents looks like at weekends.
